## context7
Use this server to retrieve up-to-date documentation and code examples for any library.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". feat(checks): expectation-catalog expansion — the 5 high-ROI GX built-ins (mostly, compound, type, set/date) + the aggregate-stats decision
----BODY----
From [docs/post-v1-dq-intelligence-notes.md](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/docs/post-v1-dq-intelligence-notes.md) §Theme 1 (post-v1 roadmap Theme 2 — noted there as design-captured but not yet filed; this files it).

**4 of 5 are catalog-only** entries in `frontend/src/components/checks/expectationCatalog.ts` (no server-side allowlist exists — `gx_runner` title-cases any `expectation_type`):

- **`mostly`** — tolerance field on existing expectations ("95% not-null"). GX still emits `unexpected_percent`, so ADR 0016 banding is unchanged. Highest ROI / lowest cost — do first.
- **Compound / cross-column** — `expect_compound_columns_to_be_unique`, `expect_column_pair_values_a_to_be_greater_than_b`, `expect_multicolumn_sum_to_equal`.
- **Type** — `expect_column_values_to_be_of_type` / `in_type_list`.
- **Set relations / date format** — `expect_column_distinct_values_to_be_in_set` / `to_contain_set`, `expect_column_values_to_match_strftime_format`.

**The 5th — aggregate stats (`expect_column_{mean,median,sum,stdev,min,max}_to_be_between`) is a design decision, not a free add:** no `unexpected_percent`, scalar `observed_value`, two-sided. That is the monitor-kind `metric_value` shape (ADR 0012), not the GX-banded shape — decide deliberately (likely a monitor kind) before building. Note #1202 already hit the adjacent class (scalar-only observed_value ⇒ no trend/baseline).

Sequencing: this unblocks the vocabulary for LLM check suggestions and is extended by the curated-superset/allowlist work (see the notes doc's sequencing diagram).
----COMMENTS----
===== #1510 =====
feat(checks): curated expectation superset (4a) + server-side expectation_type allowlist
----BODY----
From [docs/post-v1-dq-intelligence-notes.md](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/docs/post-v1-dq-intelligence-notes.md) §Theme 4 (roadmap Theme 2; filed per the roadmap's 'file from the detail doc when picked up' note).

**Chosen scope is 4a:** a vetted, server-served superset of GX's ~50 built-ins — the existing catalog pattern scaled up. **Explicitly not 4b** (an open marketplace of arbitrary/community `Expectation` classes — a code-execution / supply-chain risk; such classes would have to be image-installed, pinned and reviewed, never loaded dynamically).

**The useful irony is the real deliverable:** doing 4a safely means adding the **server-side allowlist v1 deliberately lacks** — today `gx_runner` title-cases *any* `expectation_type` string into a GX class and `checks.config` is free-form JSONB. Flip that convenience into a vetted catalog the backend validates submitted `expectation_type`s against. This also hardens LLM-generated output (SQL-gen / suggestions issues) and MCP `create_check`/`update_check`/`import_suite` inputs.

Depends on / extends #1509 (the built-ins batch).
----COMMENTS----
===== #1551 =====
Suites check-list card is too thin — missing engine, dimension, and severity thresholds
----BODY----
## What
#1550 added the engine (gx/dmf) picker to the check editor and version-history drawer. The suite's check-list card and result-detail surfaces don't show several fields a user would want at a glance:

- `frontend/src/pages/Suites.tsx` — the check-list item renders raw `check.expectation_type` but never `check.engine`, `check.dimension` (ADR 0038), or the warn/fail/critical thresholds. Two `monitor:freshness` checks on the same suite (one gx, one dmf) render identically; a check's DQ dimension and the value it goes warn/fail/critical at are both invisible without opening its edit form.
- `frontend/src/pages/RunDetail.tsx` and `frontend/src/components/results/RunReport.tsx` — both the interactive run-detail table and the printable PDF report show `expectation_type`/`kind` per result row, never `engine`. Triaging a failed freshness check, there's no way to tell "GX read the data out and computed staleness" from "Snowflake DMF computed it natively in-warehouse" without opening the check editor separately — a materially different debugging context (DMF failures skew warehouse/permission issues, GX failures skew batch-resolution issues).

## Why not fixed in #1550
Visibility polish across multiple result-rendering surfaces, not a correctness bug — scoped out to keep that PR to the picker + its direct consequences (version-history restore safety, which *was* a correctness issue).

## Fix
Add engine/dimension/threshold badges to the Suites check-list item, reusing the `ENGINE_LABEL` map pattern from `CheckHistoryDrawer.tsx` for engine; add an engine badge to the RunDetail/RunReport result rows.

## Found via
Backend↔frontend parity audit (session 2026-08-22) confirmed this is still open and broadened the scope to dimension + thresholds (findings #3/#4, alongside #1554/#1555).
----COMMENTS----
===== #1505 =====
v1 API silently ignores unknown request fields (extra='ignore') — an invented knob validates cleanly and does nothing
----BODY----
## Found by

The #1412 investigation (W7-stretch burn-down, 2026-08-21). The qa-verifier's scenario 53 probed dry-run with a `target_override` field and observed it inert — the investigation showed the field **does not exist and never has** (`git log -S target_override` over the full history: zero code hits). What scenario 53 actually observed is that `ApiModel` inherits Pydantic's default `extra='ignore'`: any unknown top-level key in any v1 request body validates cleanly and is silently dropped.

Proven at the boundary:

```python
CheckDryRunRequest.model_validate({... , 'target_override': {'table': 'FAKE.TABLE'}})
# → validates OK; key silently dropped
```

## Why it matters

This is the API-surface twin of the MCP honesty findings (#1444 class): a client that misspells a field (`warn_treshold`), or invents one from a plausible mental model (exactly what the QA agent did), gets a 200 and behavior indistinguishable from the field working — the 'inert knob' shape (the #529 review's `window_days` lesson: a knob that does nothing will be used, and then a difference that isn't there will be explained). `Settings` already runs `extra='forbid'` for the same reason (#209).

## Why not fixed inline

`extra='forbid'` on `ApiModel` is the natural fix and `_base.py` is the right seam ('cross-cutting input contracts live in exactly one place'), but it is shared by **response** models — safe for `from_attributes` construction (attributes mode never applies forbid) but any handler that builds a response via `model_validate(dict)` with surplus keys would start 500ing. Flipping it needs an audit of every response-model construction plus a breaking-change note for API/PAT clients that send extra keys. That is its own PR with its own review, not a bolt-on to a closeout item.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide forbid-vs-ignore deliberately (likely: `extra='forbid'` on request models — split `ApiRequestModel`/`ApiModel` or audit response constructions)
- [ ] Regression test: an unknown top-level field in a request body → 422 naming the field
- [ ] CHANGELOG note (breaking for clients sending unknown fields)

Refs #1412.
----COMMENTS----
===== #1326 =====
test: migration-parity literal-set check can't distinguish IS NULL from IS NOT NULL
----BODY----
Filed per the working agreement: review findings deferred from a PR are tracked, never silently dropped. Surfaced by \`/code-review\` on #1322 (the #323 retention-sweep index/batch PR).

## The gap

\`backend/tests/db/test_migration_parity.py::test_vocabularies_in_predicates_match_between_model_and_database\` compares partial-index and CHECK-constraint predicates between the SQLAlchemy model and a migration-built database by extracting the set of **quoted string literals** (\`_literals()\`, a regex over \`'...'\`) from each side and diffing the sets.

This misses drift where the predicate's *logic* changes but no literal moves. Concretely: if a future edit inverted \`sample_failures_purged_at IS NULL\` to \`sample_failures_purged_at IS NOT NULL\` on either the model's \`postgresql_where=text(...)\` or the migration's raw SQL — but not both — the literal-set comparison would still pass, because neither clause contains a quoted string literal at all. The same blind spot applies to any predicate built entirely from IS [NOT] NULL / comparison operators with no string literal operand.

## Why it matters here

\`ix_results_unpurged_created\` (added in #1322) has exactly this shape — \`sample_failures_purged_at IS NULL AND sample_failures IS NOT NULL AND jsonb_typeof(sample_failures) <> 'null'\`. The \`'null'\` literal is covered, but the two \`IS [NOT] NULL\` clauses are not: an inversion on one side only would silently pass this test while the index diverges from what the sweep's query actually needs (or from what the model claims), reintroducing the F1/F2-shaped class of bug #1322 exists to close — the sweep quietly stops benefiting from the index it doesn't do a full-scan seq-scan check on.

## Suggested fix

Extend \`test_vocabularies_in_predicates_match_between_model_and_database\` (or add a sibling check) to also normalize and compare the full predicate expression tree — or at minimum extract \`IS [NOT] NULL\` clauses (and other literal-free comparison shapes) the same way \`_literals()\` extracts quoted strings, so a bare polarity flip is caught. The module's own docstring already frames this as "the drift \`compare_metadata\` cannot see" — this is the same category of gap the module exists to close, just not yet covered for this specific predicate shape.

## Not blocking

The two indexes as shipped in #1322 were verified correct in prod-shape by hand (a real \`\d results\` inspection + a live \`EXPLAIN ANALYZE\` proving both halves hit their intended index) — this is a hardening request for the *automated* safety net catching a future regression, not a report of a current defect.
----COMMENTS----
===== #1320 =====
feat(suites): suite-delete confirmation must state its blast radius (N checks / runs / results destroyed)
----BODY----
From ADR [0041](../blob/main/docs/adr/0041-history-audit-strategy.md) §2 decision 3 — this is the mitigation that makes re-deferring soft-delete honest rather than a bare "no".

## Problem

`DELETE /api/v1/suites/{id}` cascades **checks → runs → results** (`runs.suite_id` and `results.check_id`/`run_id` are all `ON DELETE CASCADE` since #540). There is no soft-delete, no retention copy, and no undo: a suite with two years of run history is destroyed by one confirmation dialog that says nothing about it.

This is the one place where ADR 0020's accepted cascade posture still costs real, irreplaceable data — the connection half was closed by the #753 409 guard (a connection with suites simply cannot be deleted), leaving suite deletion as the only path to silent history loss.

ADR 0041 re-defers soft-delete for good reasons (a `deleted_at IS NULL` predicate across an asset/lineage/incident/rollup query surface; "deleted means inert" for live SecretStore credentials, trigger bindings and schedules; and a delete-that-does-not-delete working against #432/G2 erasure). What it does **not** defend is the user finding out afterwards.

## Fix

Make the blast radius explicit **before** the fact:

- `GET /suites/{id}` (or a small dedicated endpoint) returns the dependent counts: checks, runs, results, plus whether any trigger binding or schedule points at the suite.
- The delete confirmation states them plainly — e.g. *"Deletes 12 checks, 431 runs and 5,180 results. This cannot be undone."* — rather than the current generic confirm.
- Counts are computed, never estimated; if a count is capped for cost, say so (no silent caps).

Deliberately **not** in scope: undo, soft-delete, archive/export-on-delete. Those re-open ADR 0041 §2.3.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dependent counts (checks / runs / results / trigger bindings / schedules) available to the frontend for a suite the caller may delete
- [ ] Suite delete confirmation shows the counts and states that it is irreversible
- [ ] Authz unchanged — counts follow the same grant as the delete itself, no leak to a `view`-only user
- [ ] Test: a suite with runs shows non-zero counts; a never-run suite shows zeros and does not degrade to a scary-but-empty warning

----COMMENTS----

# Post-v1 notes — Expectation expansion, marketplace & LLM-assisted authoring (deferred design)

> **Status: deferred to post-v1 — now filed as discrete backlog issues (2026-08-21):**
> [#1509](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1509) (Theme 1 — the 5 GX
> built-ins + the aggregate-stats decision) ·
> [#1510](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1510) (Theme 4a — curated
> superset + the server-side allowlist) ·
> [#1511](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1511) (the `LLMProvider`
> seam — the shared enabler) ·
> [#1512](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1512) (Theme 2 — LLM
> SQL generator) · [#1513](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1513)
> (Theme 3 — LLM check suggestions).
> Captured so the design intent isn't lost. None of
> this is a v1 blocker — the v1 DQ loop (checks → results → trends → freshness/volume
> monitors → alerts → MCP) stands on its own. These are the "intelligence" layer on
> top of it.
>
> **The big enabler (already true in v1):** there is **no server-side expectation
> allowlist** — [`gx_runner`](../backend/app/datasources/gx_runner.py) title-cases *any*
> `expectation_type` string into a GX class, and `checks.config` is free-form JSONB.
> So "add an expectation" / "wire in a check" is mostly a **frontend-catalog + config-
> validation** problem, not a backend-engine one. That's why the items below are
> cheaper than they look.

## The four themes

### 1. Implement the 5 high-ROI GX built-ins
**Feasibility: High · Effort: S–M · No new infra.**

- **4 of 5 are catalog-only** entries in
  [`frontend/src/components/checks/expectationCatalog.ts`](../frontend/src/components/checks/expectationCatalog.ts):
  - **`mostly`** — tolerance on any existing expectation ("95% not-null"). One optional
    field; GX still emits `unexpected_percent`, so it bands under ADR 0016 unchanged.
    **Highest ROI / lowest cost** — do first.
  - **Compound / cross-column** — `expect_compound_columns_to_be_unique` (multi-column
    primary keys), `expect_column_pair_values_a_to_be_greater_than_b` (e.g.
    `end_date > start_date`), `expect_multicolumn_sum_to_equal`.
  - **Type** — `expect_column_values_to_be_of_type` / `in_type_list`.
  - **Set relations / date format** — `expect_column_distinct_values_to_be_in_set` /
    `to_contain_set`, `expect_column_values_to_match_strftime_format`.
- **The 5th — aggregate stats** (`expect_column_{mean,median,sum,stdev,min,max}_to_be_between`)
  is the **design decision, not a free add.** They don't emit `unexpected_percent`; the
  result is a **scalar in `observed_value`** and they're **two-sided** (too low *or* too
  high fails). That's the *volume-monitor* shape, not the GX unexpected-% shape — so
  aggregates likely belong on the **monitor-kind `metric_value` path** (ADR 0012, the
  freshness/volume engine, #426) as a 3rd monitor kind, **not** as a GX-banded
  expectation. Decide deliberately before building.

### 2. LLM SQL generator for custom-SQL checks (`UnexpectedRowsExpectation`)
**Feasibility: High · Effort: M · Best-aligned of the four.**

- NL rule → LLM-generated SQL → existing **custom-SQL guardrails** (ADR 0019:
  read-only single-statement validation + SQL-datasource gating + least-privilege role)

# Longest string allowed anywhere in an expectation config (keys AND values).

# The reported path/type in a 422 is bounded too — the error envelope is echoed

def _find_oversized_string(value: Any, path: str = "config") -> str | None:
    """Depth-first search for a string over the cap (dict keys included);
    returns its (bounded) path, or None.
    """
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return path if len(value) > _CONFIG_STRING_MAX_CHARS else None
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        for key, item in value.items():
            # str() first: JSON transports only produce string keys, but a
            # direct Python caller may not — slicing an int key would TypeError.
            key_repr = str(key)[:_ERROR_ECHO_MAX_CHARS]
            if isinstance(key, str) and len(key) > _CONFIG_STRING_MAX_CHARS:
                return f"{path}.{key_repr}… (key)"
            found = _find_oversized_string(item, f"{path}.{key_repr}")
            if found:
                return found
    if isinstance(value, list):
        for i, item in enumerate(value):
            found = _find_oversized_string(item, f"{path}[{i}]")
            if found:
                return found
    return None

    """Author-time validation for `kind='expectation'` checks (#651)."""
    _reject_oversized_config(config)

    # Lazy: importing great_expectations is heavy (seconds), and the API process
    # only needs it on the authoring paths — same pattern as the vault client.
    import great_expectations.expectations as gxe
    from great_expectations.expectations.expectation import Expectation

    from backend.app.datasources.gx_runner import _expectation_class_name

    class_name = _expectation_class_name(expectation_type)
    expectation_cls = getattr(gxe, class_name, None)
    # The issubclass guard keeps a crafted type from resolving to a non-expectation
    # module attribute via the title-casing getattr.
    if expectation_cls is None or not (
        isinstance(expectation_cls, type) and issubclass(expectation_cls, Expectation)
    ):
        # Bounded echo: REST caps expectation_type at 128 chars, but the MCP tools don't — never
        # round-trip an unbounded string through the 422 envelope and the error log.
        raise CheckConfigInvalidError(
            f"unknown expectation_type {expectation_type[:_ERROR_ECHO_MAX_CHARS]!r} — "
            "not a Great Expectations expectation",
            detail={"expectation_type": expectation_type[:_ERROR_ECHO_MAX_CHARS]},
        )
    try:
        expectation_cls(**config)
    except Exception as exc:
        # pydantic ValidationError (missing/wrong-typed/extra kwargs) or a GX

        raise CheckConfigInvalidError(

    """Append an immutable snapshot of `check`'s current state as its next version (a per-check
    sequence starting at 1). The caller commits — this only adds the row, so the snapshot and
    the create/update it records commit atomically.
    """
    # MAX over no rows is NULL → None; `or 0` makes the first version 1.
    current_max = session.scalar(
        select(func.max(CheckVersion.version_no)).where(CheckVersion.check_id == check.id)
    )
    next_no = (current_max or 0) + 1
    version = CheckVersion(
        check_id=check.id,
        version_no=next_no,
        name=check.name,
        kind=check.kind,
        engine=check.engine,
        expectation_type=check.expectation_type,
        dimension=check.dimension,
        source_connection_id=check.source_connection_id,
        config=check.config,
        warn_threshold=check.warn_threshold,
        fail_threshold=check.fail_threshold,
        critical_threshold=check.critical_threshold,
        changed_by=actor_id,
    )
    session.add(version)
    return version

Research done. Here's the picture and the plan, then I'm starting execution.

## W2 pending items (6 open in milestone `v1.2 Week 2`, due 2026-09-04)

Key research finding: the notes' "no server-side allowlist" claim is **stale** — `validate_expectation_check` (#651) already rejects non-GX types and bad configs at [check_service.py:557](backend/app/services/check_service.py#L557). What #1510 actually adds is narrowing "any of GX's ~50 built-ins" to a **curated allowlist**. The catalog today has only 8 GX entries and no `mostly` support anywhere.

## Ranking (priority × dependencies)

| Rank | Issue | Why | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | #1509 catalog expansion (mostly, compound, type-list, set/date) + aggregate-stats decision | Exit-gate core; unblocks #1510 and the W3/W4 LLM vocabulary | — |
| 2 | #1510 curated superset + server-side allowlist | Exit-gate core; security-labeled; hardens REST/MCP/import + future LLM output | #1509 |
| 3 | #1320 suite-delete blast radius | Only remaining path to silent history loss (ADR 0041 mitigation) | — |
| 4 | #1505 `extra='forbid'` on request models | Exit-gate ("decided/landed"); breaking-change audit needed | — |
| 5 | #1326 migration-parity IS [NOT] NULL | Small test hardening, independent | — |
| 6 | #1551 check-card engine/dimension/threshold badges | Polish; touches Suites.tsx → sequenced after #1320 to avoid conflicts | after #1320 merges |

**Additional issue needed:** yes, one — the #1509 aggregate-stats decision resolves (per the notes' own analysis) to "monitor-kind `metric_value` path, not GX-banded", which needs a follow-up build issue in `v1.2 Backlog`. Filing it now.

## TODO / execution plan

- [ ] File aggregate-stats monitor-kind follow-up issue (backlog)
- [ ] **Batch 1 (parallel worktrees):** #1509 (opus) · #1320 (sonnet) · #1326 (sonnet)

You are working in a git worktree of the DataQ repo (FastAPI backend). Read CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md first. Implement GitHub issue #1326 (repo TheurgicDuke771/DataQ): the migration-parity literal-set check can't distinguish IS NULL from IS NOT NULL. Read the issue body (`gh issue view 1326`) — it names the exact test and gap.

WHAT TO BUILD:
In backend/tests/db/test_migration_parity.py, `test_vocabularies_in_predicates_match_between_model_and_database` compares partial-index/CHECK predicates between the SQLAlchemy models and a migration-built DB by diffing sets of quoted string literals (`_literals()` regex). Literal-free clauses like `sample_failures_purged_at IS NULL` are invisible to it — a polarity flip to IS NOT NULL on one side only passes silently. Fix per the issue's suggested approach: alongside `_literals()`, extract normalized `<column> IS [NOT] NULL` clauses (and ideally other literal-free comparison shapes present in the predicates, e.g. `jsonb_typeof(...) <> '...'` is literal-covered already — focus on IS [NOT] NULL polarity) from both sides and compare those sets too. Normalize whitespace/case/quoting consistently between the model's `postgresql_where=text(...)` strings and what Postgres reports back (pg reformats predicates — inspect what the DB side actually returns for `ix_results_unpurged_created` and normalize both sides to a canonical form; watch for pg wrapping column names in parens or adding casts).

PROOF REQUIREMENT (the standing "prove the test can FAIL" rule): after the fix, mutation-check it — temporarily flip one IS NULL to IS NOT NULL in the extraction input on one side (or simulate via a targeted unit test of the extractor with a flipped predicate pair) and show the assertion goes red for the RIGHT reason. Include the proof description in the PR body. Prefer also adding a small direct unit test of the new extractor function on flipped-polarity fixture strings so the failure mode is permanently pinned.

CONVENTIONS (mandatory):
- Test-only change; touch only backend/tests/db/test_migration_parity.py (plus helpers within it).
- Comments minimal (~0.2 prose-to-code).
- The parity tests need a real Postgres — check how they run locally (docker-compose Postgres; look at the test module's fixtures/markers and backend/tests/db/README or conftest). Run them for real: `conda run -n dataq pytest backend/tests/db/test_migration_parity.py -q` with the compose Postgres up (`docker-compose up -d postgres` if needed — do NOT restart/stop already-running services). Also run black/ruff/mypy on the file: mypy must be the full `mypy backend` sweep.
- Branch `fix/issue-1326-parity-null-polarity` off main; conventional commit `test(db): migration-parity check catches IS [NOT] NULL polarity drift (#1326)`.
- Push, open PR via `gh pr create` following .github/pull_request_template.md, body includes `Fixes #1326` + the mutation-proof description, set milestone "v1.2 Week 2 — expectation catalog + server-side allowlist". DO NOT merge.

<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>## Findings

1. **Multi-word cast types silently mis-attribute the column (real bug).** `(?:::\w+)?` only consumes a single word after `::`, so a cast like `::character varying` or `::timestamp without time zone` isn't fully consumed. The regex then re-anchors on the trailing word of the cast as if it were the column name. Verified: `_null_polarities("(col)::character varying IS NULL")` → `{('varying', False)}` — it loses `col` entirely and reports a bogus `varying` column. Plausible in Postgres-generated predicate text (multi-word type names are common), and would cause silent false-negative/false-positive drift results. **Confidence: medium-high.**

2. **String literals aren't excluded from scanning (real, lower-impact bug).** The regex has no literal-string awareness, so any single word immediately preceding `IS [NOT] NULL` inside a quoted string literal gets picked up as a "column." Verified: `_null_polarities("col <> 'some value IS NULL text'")` → `{('value', False)}`, a spurious clause. Whether this occurs in practice depends on whether any real CHECK/index predicate embeds such literal text next to that phrasing — currently none do in the tested cases, so real-world risk is low. **Confidence: low-medium.**

3. **`NOT (col IS NULL)` wrapping form isn't recognized as a polarity flip** — only the bare-keyword `IS NOT NULL` form is detected. In practice Postgres always normalizes/stores `IS NOT NULL` rather than `NOT (... IS NULL)`, so this is likely moot for `pg_get_constraintdef`/`indexdef` output. **Confidence: low** (design limitation, not likely a live bug given Postgres's own canonicalization).

No issues found with group indices, `bool(is_not)` truthiness logic, the `model_sql`/`live[name]` variable scoping in the modified test, or the two new unit tests' expected values — all check out correctly against the regex as implemented.</result>

<result>Good, this confirms the shape. I have enough to give a confident, evidence-grounded finding.

## Findings

1. **`NOT (col IS NULL)` wrapping is mis-normalized — false-negative risk.** `_null_polarities` requires the literal `NOT` to sit immediately before `NULL`; it has no concept of an outer `NOT(...)` wrapping the whole clause. Tested against the actual regex: `NOT (sample_failures_purged_at IS NULL)` normalizes to `(col, False)` — identical to a plain `IS NULL`, i.e. it reads as the opposite polarity from what it means. This is exactly the class of drift the PR exists to catch (per its own docstring: "the exact regression `_literals()` cannot see"), just one level deeper — a migration author writing `WHERE NOT (col IS NULL)` instead of `col IS NOT NULL` would slip past both the old and new checks. **Confidence: high** (verified against the actual regex).

2. **The generalized bug class — IN/NOT IN, LIKE/NOT LIKE, `=`/`<>` — is left wide open.** `_literals()`'s blind spot isn't specific to `IS NULL`; any polarity-flippable operator whose operand set is unchanged escapes literal-diffing the same way. The model already contains exactly these shapes: `_in_check()` emits `col IN (...)` (models.py:120-122, used by `type_valid`/`role_valid`/etc.), and `uq_runs_suite_triggered_by`'s partial index uses `LIKE '...%'` chains. A future `IN`→`NOT IN` or `LIKE`→`NOT LIKE` flip on either side would reproduce #1326's exact silent-pass failure mode, and this PR's fix is narrowly scoped to `IS [NOT] NULL` only. **Confidence: medium-high** (the shapes exist in the model today; no incident yet, but the PR's own rationale generalizes to them).

3. **`IS DISTINCT FROM NULL` is invisible to the extractor** (falls out of the regex entirely, contributing nothing to either set) — a semantically-equivalent-to-`IS [NOT] NULL` construct that wouldn't currently trigger a false positive only because it isn't used anywhere in the codebase yet. **Confidence: low** (no precedent in current code; purely a latent gap).

No issues found with the core normalization logic for the shapes it does target (parens, casts, `comparison_source_presence`'s boolean-equality form) — tested against plausible Postgres reformatting and it holds up correctly.</result>

**Issue 1 — comment's cast-tolerance justification doesn't match its own example; the cast branch is untested (medium-high confidence).**
Comment: *"a cast may sit beside an unrelated comparison in the same clause — so tolerate surrounding parens/casts around the column but still require the literal `IS [NOT] NULL` keywords."*
The cited example (`jsonb_typeof(sample_failures) <> 'null'::text`) has the cast on a string *literal* inside an unrelated `<>` comparison — it never sits next to the null-tested column and never reaches the `(?:::\w+)?` branch of `_NULL_CLAUSE` at all (verified: the regex never matches that clause since it lacks `IS`). So the stated rationale doesn't actually motivate or exercise the "tolerate casts around the column" behavior it's attached to. I confirmed against a live migrated DB (`docker exec` Postgres, `alembic upgrade head`, then `pg_get_constraintdef`/`pg_indexes`) that none of the four real `IS [NOT] NULL` predicates in the schema (`ck_incidents_incident_resolved_by_valid`, `ck_checks_comparison_source_presence`, `uq_lineage_edges_up_down_source_nullconn`, `ix_results_unpurged_created`) ever put a cast directly on the null-tested column — so the `(?:::\w+)?` branch is currently dead code, and neither of the two new unit tests (`test_null_polarities_normalizes_...`, `test_null_polarities_catches_a_polarity_flip`) exercises it either.

**Issue 2 — latent regex bug in the untested cast branch (lower confidence, speculative since no current predicate hits it).**
Because Issue 1's branch is untested, a real gap is unverified: `(?:::\w+)?` only matches single-word cast type names. A Postgres rendering like `(col)::character varying IS NULL` (space in the type name) would fail to match, silently dropping that column from `_null_polarities()` and defeating the drift check for it — directly undermining the module's stated purpose. Not currently triggered (all live predicates checked have single-word or no casts), but it's exactly the class of edge case the comment claims is handled ("tolerate ... casts around the column") and isn't proven.

No other inconsistencies found — the main test's docstring, `_null_polarities()`'s docstring, and the `_live_predicates`/module docstrings all accurately describe what the code does, and both new tests do pass against a real migrated Postgres instance (verified via `pytest backend/tests/db/test_migration_parity.py`, 4 passed).</result>

Implement GitHub issue #1505 (repo TheurgicDuke771/DataQ): the v1 API silently ignores unknown request fields (`extra='ignore'`). Read the issue (`gh issue view 1505`) — it has the analysis and acceptance criteria.

THE DECISION (already made in the issue's AC — implement it): `extra='forbid'` on REQUEST models only. The shared base is `ApiModel` in backend/app/api/v1/_base.py:42, used by both request and response models, so:
1. Add `ApiRequestModel(ApiModel)` with `model_config` extending the base config with `extra='forbid'` (check how ApiModel's model_config is declared and extend correctly — Pydantic v2 ConfigDict merge semantics: child model_config shallow-merges over parent).
2. Audit every request-body model across backend/app/api/v1/*.py (anything used as a POST/PATCH/PUT body parameter — grep the route signatures) and rebase them onto ApiRequestModel. Response models stay on ApiModel. Be careful with models used for BOTH (if any exist, split them or leave on ApiModel with a note in the PR body listing them and why).
3. Audit risk area from the issue: any handler building a RESPONSE via `model_validate(dict)` with surplus keys would 500 under forbid — that's why you only flip request models. Verify no request model is also constructed server-side from dicts with surplus keys (grep for `<ModelName>.model_validate(` and `<ModelName>(` constructions of the request classes); fix call sites if any.
4. Nested request sub-models: a forbid on the top-level model does not cover nested `ApiModel` sub-models — move nested request-only sub-models to ApiRequestModel too (e.g. connection config sub-objects, check config wrappers if typed — note `checks.config` is deliberately free-form JSONB `dict[str, Any]`, leave it free-form; the tolerance is validated in the service layer).
5. Regression tests: an unknown top-level field in a request body → 422 naming the field (parametrize over several representative routes: create suite, create check, create connection, dry-run — the issue's own probe was `target_override` on dry-run); a misspelled field like `warn_treshold` → 422. Also one test that a nested request sub-model rejects unknown keys. And prove response serialization still works (existing tests cover this — run the full suite).
6. CHANGELOG note (find the changelog: docs/site/changelog.md) — breaking for API/PAT clients sending unknown fields; state it plainly.
7. MCP surface note: MCP tools take explicit kwargs, not Pydantic request bodies — confirm nothing in backend/app/mcp/server.py routes raw dicts through these request models in a way that would now 422 (grep for the request model names in mcp/). If dryrun/create paths construct request models from tool args, ensure they don't pass surplus keys.

- Comments minimal (~0.2 prose-to-code).
- Conda env `dataq`; verify locally before commit: `conda run -n dataq black --check backend && conda run -n dataq ruff check backend && conda run -n dataq mypy backend && conda run -n dataq pytest backend/tests -q` (full suite — this change can break far-flung tests that POST surplus keys; fix any test that was accidentally relying on ignore semantics, and treat each such failure as signal: if a FRONTEND call site sends a surplus key, that's a real defect to fix in the frontend too — grep frontend/src/api for the affected payloads).

- Never commit credentials. Clean up any scratch files before committing.

Note: I did **not** merge it — I left it open per instructions. Issue #1326 auto-closed as a result.

**Follow-up issue filed:** [#1605](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1605) (milestone `v1.2 Backlog`) — extending the literal-free/polarity-flippable-operator class to `IN`/`NOT IN`, `LIKE`/`NOT LIKE`, and `IS DISTINCT FROM NULL`.

## What was built

In `backend/tests/db/test_migration_parity.py`:
- Added `_null_polarities(sql)`, a sibling to `_literals()` that extracts `{(column, is_not_null)}` from every `<column> IS [NOT] NULL` clause, tolerating Postgres's read-back reformatting (extra parens, `::type` casts) and an outer `NOT (...)` wrap.
- `test_vocabularies_in_predicates_match_between_model_and_database` now diffs the null-polarity sets alongside the literal sets.
- Four pinned unit tests requiring no database: normalization equivalence, the original polarity-flip regression, a multi-word-cast regression, and an outer-`NOT` regression.

**Normalization approach:** captured real predicate text from a live scratch database (`alembic upgrade head` + `pg_get_constraintdef`/`pg_indexes`) for every CHECK/partial-index in the model to see exactly how Postgres reformats each shape, then built the regex against that ground truth rather than guessing.

## Review cycle

`/code-review` (5 parallel agents) found 3 real bugs in the first version, all fixed in a `fixup:` commit ([`42049801`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/commit/420498015d99d3a20ecbcfd5e80539edc851dc21)):
1. Single-word-only cast regex re-anchored on a multi-word type name's trailing word (`(col)::character varying IS NULL` → wrongly extracted `{('varying', False)}`).
2. `NOT (col IS NULL)` read as the opposite polarity (only the inner clause was inspected).
3. A stale comment cited an example that didn't actually reach the cast branch.

Both bugs were mutation-checked against the pre-fix regex (confirmed failing) and against the fix (confirmed passing). A 4th finding (IN/LIKE/DISTINCT-FROM generalization) was filed as #1605 rather than built, since it's out of #1326's scope. A 5th (no quote-awareness in the extractor) was recorded as verified-benign in the extractor's docstring and the PR body — same accepted class `_literals()` already has, no current predicate triggers it.

## Verification

- `TEST_DATABASE_URL=... conda run -n dataq pytest backend/tests/db/test_migration_parity.py -q --no-cov` → 6 passed, against the real compose Postgres.
- `black --check`, `ruff check` on the file: clean.
- Full `mypy backend` sweep (455 source files): clean.
- Mutation-proof (both rounds): temporarily flipped `sample_failures_purged_at IS NULL` → `IS NOT NULL` in `backend/app/db/models.py` only, confirmed the DB-integration test fails with the exact polarity mismatch message, then reverted (verified via `git diff`/`git status` that `models.py` ended up unmodified — this PR is test-only as required).
- All 14 CI checks on the PR passed (backend/frontend lint, type check, tests, Playwright E2E, Bandit, CodeQL, pip-audit/pnpm audit, secret scanning).

## Deferred

Nothing outstanding from this issue's scope. The one deliberate deferral is #1605 (broader operator-polarity class), filed rather than built.</result>

## PR #1608 — https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1608

Branch `feature/1509-expectation-catalog-expansion`, 6 commits, 19 files (+1051/−42). Milestone set to *v1.2 Week 2*. **Full CI green (15/15). Not merged.**

### What shipped, per group

1. **`mostly`** — optional 0–1 tolerance on the seven row-wise expectations GX accepts it on (not-null, unique, between, in-set, value-lengths, regex, of-type). Not on row-count or the two distinct-value relations, where GX rejects the kwarg. ADR 0016 banding is unchanged, and that is *executed* rather than asserted: the three variants run through the real runner and `unexpected_percent` stays 20.0 while GX's `success` moves. The help text states the consequence — a threshold below the tolerance still bands a run GX passed, because `derive_status` reads the metric, not `success`. A `step` field was added to `ConfigField` (antd's default step of 1 makes a 0–1 range unusable).

2. **Compound / cross-column** — `expect_compound_columns_to_be_unique` (uniqueness), `expect_column_pair_values_a_to_be_greater_than_b` (with `or_equal`), `expect_multicolumn_sum_to_equal`.

3. **Type list** — `expect_column_values_to_be_in_type_list`, sharing #768's `typeFieldHint` via a `TYPE_FIELD_NAMES` set.

4. **Set relations / date format** — `expect_column_distinct_values_to_{be_in,contain}_set` and `expect_column_values_to_match_strftime_format`.

5. **Aggregate stats deliberately not built** — recorded in the PR body and changelog, tracked as **#1602**.

Backend `check_dimension` derivation extended for all seven (the existing contract test asserts both directions and would have failed otherwise). Pair/sum are **validity**, not consistency — ADR 0038 scopes consistency to agreement between related *datasets*, and these are single-row rules; `contain_set` is **completeness**.

### Two findings the build produced (both fixed in-PR)

- **`expect_column_values_to_match_strftime_format` can never run on Snowflake.** GX registers its metric for Pandas/Spark only and the class doesn't override `_validate` the way the type checks do — verified by running it, it raises `No provider found` on a SQL batch. The ADR-0019-on-UC shape exactly. Gated twice: the editor drops it per-*spec* (new `dataframeOnly` flag + `runsSqlBatch`), and `reject_dataframe_only_expectation` 422s it at author time on create, update **and suite import**. UC still offers it (its pushdown set is an allowlist, so it routes to the pandas batch).
- **Severity bands are inert on the two distinct-value relations** — they compare a set, so there's no `unexpected_percent` for `extract_metric`. Documented where the bands are entered; the stronger `noThresholds` + backend-rejection treatment needs live-warehouse confirmation, so **filed as #1607**.

### Tests

~40 new assertions. Backend: a new `test_catalog_expectation_runs.py` that runs **every** GX catalog type through the real `gx_runner` on both a pandas and a SQLAlchemy batch (a `_RUN_SAMPLES` guard fails when a catalog entry is added without a runnable sample); a parametrized test proving the DataFrame-only type genuinely errors on SQL, so the exclusion is a measured fact and goes red if GX ever adds the provider; 5 API gate tests (create/update/import, plus the allow cases). Frontend: 26 new tests across catalog/checkForm/gating. Suite totals **5023 backend @ 97.12%**, **1161 frontend @ 91.23% lines**.

### `/code-review` — four findings, all fixed, none deferred

Highest was real and mine: **suite import bypassed the gate** (it builds `Check(...)` directly, never calling `create_check`), so a strftime check could be imported onto Snowflake, error forever, and then refuse every PATCH that would fix it. Fixed by re-shaping the gate to take a connection type instead of a `Suite`, so one function serves all three doors (MCP's `import_suite` came along for free). Also: the UC routing guard asserted a *union*, hiding a set overlap that would have kept every test green while breaking UC runs — disjointness now asserted; `mostly` floored at 0.01 rather than GX's 0 (`mostly=0` succeeds unconditionally = #426 silent green); and the picker gate now fails **closed** on an unknown connection type, like every sibling gate. Full reply posted at [comment](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1608#issuecomment-5454853661).

### Deviations / things to know

- **The three cross-column types are not live-verified on Snowflake or Databricks SQL.** The SQL proof is sqlite — provider *presence* is engine-class-level so that part is sound, but a dialect-specific compilation failure wouldn't show up. Called out explicitly in the PR body; worth one live run per the #953 rule before this reaches prod.
- All seven new types are deliberately routed to UC's **frame** batch, not added to `SQL_PUSHDOWN_EXPECTATION_TYPES` — that list is an audited set and nothing here has been exercised against live Databricks SQL. The existing partition guard forced each to pick a side.
- Cross-column entries went into the existing **'Column values'** category rather than a new one — they're row-wise, emit `unexpected_percent`, and gate identically; adding a category was scope the issue didn't ask for.
- **Issue filed: #1607** (inert severity thresholds on the distinct-value set relations, milestoned to v1.2 W2). Nothing else deferred.</result>
